case-1.objects: Fix a map F:E→H, a field D assigning a continuous real linear map D(w):E→H to each w∈E, real bounds M₁,M₂, and a target y∈H. On the unit sphere S, K(w)=F(w) using the underlying ambient vector, and c(w,u)=arccos⟨w,u⟩ℝ. For a measure μ on S set m(μ)=∫ₛ K dμ (Bochner integral), a_μ(w)=D(w)*[m(μ)−y] using the Hilbert adjoint, V_μ(w)=2⟨m(μ)−y,F(w)⟩ℝ, and G_μ(w)=2[a_μ(w)−⟨a_μ(w),w⟩ℝw]. Q(μ,ν) is the infimum over couplings of μ and ν of the extended integral of ofReal(c(w,u)²).
case-1.domains: E and H are real inner-product spaces with their normed additive commutative group structures; E is finite-dimensional and has its Borel measurable structure, and H is complete, with no finite-dimensionality requirement on H. S is the subtype of E given by ‖w‖=1 with its induced measurable structure; K:S→H, c:S×S→ℝ, and μ and ν are measures on S. The mean lies in H, V_μ:E→ℝ and G_μ:E→E are defined on the whole ambient space, and Q takes values in [0,∞]. The derivative bounds use the closed unit ball of E, not just S.
case-1.quantifiers: For every choice of E,H with the indicated structures, every F,D and all M₁,M₂ satisfying the hypotheses, and every y∈H, there exist real C₁,C₂>0. With that one pair fixed, for every probability μ on S, K is integrable, the stated gradient holds for every ambient w∈E, and the orthogonality and norm bound hold for every w∈S. Independently, for every pair of probabilities μ,ν on S, Q(μ,ν) is finite and the two-point estimate holds for every w,u∈S. No existence of a unit vector or of a probability measure on S is assumed or asserted; in particular the measure-quantified clauses are vacuous if S is empty.
case-1.assumptions: For every w∈E, F has genuine ambient Fréchet derivative D(w) at w. The real numbers M₁ and M₂ are nonnegative. For every w with ‖w‖≤1 one has ‖D(w)‖≤M₁; for every w,u with ‖w‖,‖u‖≤1 one has ‖D(w)−D(u)‖≤M₂‖w−u‖, using operator norms on the left. These two bounds are not assumed outside the ball. Each measure used in a conclusion has unit total mass; y is arbitrary.
case-1.conclusion: For each probability μ on S, K is Bochner integrable with respect to μ and V_μ has ambient gradient 2D(w)*[m(μ)−y] at every w∈E. For all w∈S, ⟨w,G_μ(w)⟩ℝ=0 and ‖G_μ(w)‖≤C₁. For each pair of probabilities μ,ν, Q(μ,ν)≠∞, and for all w,u∈S, ‖G_μ(w)−G_ν(u)‖≤C₂[(Q(μ,ν)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)].
case-1.senses: The differentiability statements are actual ambient derivative and gradient claims, not formulas for totalized fallback operators. At a unit vector, G is the orthogonal projection of the ambient gradient onto w⊥; the statement gives this field's tangency and bounds on S, not an ambient bound for G or an assertion that G is the ambient gradient. The ground cost is the square of the angular distance arccos⟨w,u⟩ℝ, not the squared chord length. Couplings have the prescribed coordinate marginals, and their costs are integrated as extended nonnegative functions (an empty feasible set would give ∞). The separate finiteness clause makes the toReal of the extended square root the ordinary finite square root; toReal alone would not show this since it sends ∞ to zero. The statement neither asserts attainment of the infimum nor asserts bounds for non-probability measures.
case-1.constants: M₁,M₂ are given nonnegative derivative-control parameters, possibly zero; C₁,C₂ are strictly positive real constants chosen once for the fixed data, before any probability measures or evaluation points. C₁ bounds the size of the projected field, and C₂ is the single coefficient multiplying the sum of the square-root transport term and the angular displacement. The proposition specifies no numerical formula, optimality, or independence from the fixed data, including y, for either constant.
